scope: SOURCE/CONTRACT review of real customer assistance guides 07-12; not a live availability, production launch, storage qualification or indexing-completion claim. Paths in documents are package-relative; sourceFiles are repository-relative. This review file remains outside the indexed guides directory.

claims: DocumentKnowledgePage exposes an explicit target release, source binding, connector status, discovery, approval-backed registration, bounded preview, index, refresh, reconcile, removal and retrieval-proof controls.

The support DATA manifest declares customer-managed S3-compatible storage, deployment-only derived evidence, LIST/READ/HEAD authority, deleteSourceOnRemoval=false, .txt/configured .json input and explicit initial indexing approval.
Source approval occurs at registration in the current UI. Preview operates on a registered source; the guide does not invent pre-registration extracted preview or claim preview activates evidence.
DocumentKnowledgeController returns ACCEPTED for index and removal; DocumentKnowledgeService reconciles recorded indexing/deletion work rather than treating submission as completion.
DocumentKnowledgeService.refresh observes provider revision changes without indexing them; activate switches to a successful candidate before superseding and deleting old derived chunks.
The API runbook separates mounted non-production mechanics from customer-owned production source-storage qualification.
limitations: Only applies where the module, installed document policy, customer permissions and provisioned target are available. It does not claim every template supports arbitrary file formats.
No source files were uploaded, no storage credentials inspected and no live indexing or deletion performed for this documentation review.
Retrieval proof is evidence of source/version/chunk retrieval, not a guarantee of final answer quality or upstream freshness.

claims: Source storage, candidate/active indexing versions, retrieval proof and generated-answer quality are separate checks in the source lifecycle and UI.

SupportDocumentStatusService projects registered counts, active versions, newer candidates and observation times from the selected app's exact target/release and explicitly returns upstreamStorageProbed=false.
SupportResourceService derives document-target authority from a selected connected app, not the latest deployment release or text supplied to the model.
Connection status reports persisted synchronization observations with liveProviderProbed=false; it is distinct from document-version state.
Support app readiness uses evaluateLocal and deliveryProbed=false; deployment observations explicitly identify persisted state and liveHealthProbed=false.
The current support configuration uses bounded READ/RAG cooperation, while the shared philosophies prohibit semantic keyword routing, hidden recovery and unapproved automatic search-all.
limitations: The guide recommends manual source verification through the customer's own authorized storage access; it does not assert that support diagnostics read source contents or probe storage freshness.
A citation, retrieval proof or completed chain does not certify semantic accuracy or exhaustive coverage of a compound question.
No universal refresh schedule, answer-quality guarantee, search-all default or production availability is promised.

claims: The normal Marketplace compiler preserves accessMode/readOnly, confirmationRequired/requiresConfirmation and anonymousAllowed as separate action contract fields.
READ actions need not belong to an indexed vector space unless their actual retrieval or declared grounding contract requires it.
The generic confirmation flow submits confirmation/cancellation as a query in the current conversation and consumes the actual canonical result.
RequestConversationHandoverAction distinguishes EXPLICIT_USER_REQUEST from MODEL_RECOMMENDATION; a direct user request does not necessarily require an additional confirmation.

Specialist assistance is exposed as a READ capability and compiled workers have writePolicy=DISABLED. That boundary does not prohibit separate authorized Console operations or conversation-control actions.
Desk Action reviews require actual application-originated proposals and Reviewer permission; approval and business execution completion remain distinct.
limitations: The guide does not promise that every WRITE needs confirmation, every READ permits anonymous callers or every chat confirmation creates a review task.
Actual parameters, target authorization, results and confirmation policy belong to the installed integration; this guide creates no new action or repair authority.
Visible local confirmation state is not independent evidence that an external business effect completed; uncertain execution must not trigger an assumed-safe duplicate request.

claims: The customer conversational editor exposes specialist assistance, areas, instructions, approved knowledge sources, installed READ tools, resolution plans and bounded advanced limits.
Use changes updates the local form; Save support capabilities updates the deployment draft and explicitly says publish/apply is still required.
The Answer preview is synthetic, Sample-labeled and performs no AI or diagnostic checks.
The compiler emits native SpecialistChain resources with bounded manager decisions, worker invocations, parallelism and duration; it does not introduce a support-specific fixed ExecutionPlan engine.
The compiler validates installed READ authority, sets worker writes DISABLED, and explicitly reserves human handover to the outer conversation.
The runtime consult_specialist description permits direct answers to simple questions and exposes typed unsuccessful results instead of guaranteeing every specialist invocation succeeds.
Templates are bootstrap defaults; normal deployment configuration and versioning remain the evolution path.
limitations: Only applies to workspaces exposing the conversational Support capabilities editor and current edit permissions; it does not claim support for every behavior type.
Parallel permission is a bound for independent checks, not a guarantee that every worker will execute or that all findings will be included in a final summary.
Configuration preview and a completed execution are not a semantic correctness certificate, automatic repair or human-control transition.

claims: Desk is a shared managed service/store per hosting environment with deployment-target bindings, not a per-deployment Inbox deployment/database.
Owner, SUPPORT and REVIEWER roles are distinct. A registered identity has no queue permission until assigned; owners must explicitly assign themselves to handle conversations or reviews.
Enable LoomAI Desk reuses normal publish/apply/verification and app assignment remains an explicit separate operation when the app still references an older release.
Agents & access assigns registered verified identities to a target; staging and production assignments are distinct while multiple apps on a target share its team.
The visitor handover dialog is driven by configured intake fields and permissions, pauses AI while pending/active, and offers explicit return controls only where permitted.
Desk exposes claim, reply, return-to-AI and close with observable delivery outcomes; navigation or interruption does not itself authorize AI resumption.
Conversation close and optional external case resolve are separate commands; Action reviews are a separately enabled and authorized lifecycle.
limitations: No agent response-time promise, application-specific team assignment, universal anonymous intake or automatic availability claim is made.
The guide does not imply that every target has Desk or human-review enablement, or that owning a customer account grants conversation access.
Accepted delivery and reviewer approval are not proof of delivered messages or successful external business execution.

claims: The guide describes the implemented workflow only when Console exposes the module; transient rollout and production-launch status are deliberately kept out of indexed customer guidance.
CustomerSupportPage exposes summary, optional details/product/resources, consent, saved delivery states and a canonical embedded conversation with explicit start/check controls.
SupportRequesterService requires the exact current requester within the customer account; case visibility is not automatically granted to every account member.
SupportDiagnosticService rechecks current membership, ownership, active episode, open case and current consent before projecting selected-resource metadata.

SupportResourceService limits observations to release state, local readiness, connection sync and exact selected-app document targets; explicit false probe flags prevent live-health, HTTPS, provider or storage-freshness claims.
Changing selected resources, resolving or cancelling revokes consent; reopening neither restores it nor replays the intake. A terminal conversation can receive an explicitly created new episode.
The UI starts initial delivery in the explicit submission handler, not a mount effect; saved/uncertain/failed delivery remains visible without silently sending replacement AI turns.
limitations: Current hosting, enablement and production-launch truth must be checked outside this static guide; source review is not a new live verification.
This workflow is available only when the workspace exposes the module and the signed-in requester is authorized; it grants neither account-wide case sharing nor raw business-data access.
Revocation blocks subsequent diagnostic authorization but does not erase previously shared observations or conversation history. No staffing, SLA, retention or residency guarantee is asserted.
